title: Double down on enterprise; restructure SMB before it bleeds margin
subtitle: Board of Directors · Q3 2026 review · Decisions required on $2M reallocation and SMB ARR floor
core_message: Enterprise is funding all our growth while SMB unit economics have inverted; reallocate $2M and enforce a $50K ARR floor now.
narrative_arc: We open with the headline that Q3's beat masks a two-speed business, then diagnose why SMB economics have broken and why enterprise win rates are slipping against Beta. We land the financial case for reallocation and close by asking the board to approve the $2M shift, the ARR floor, and the competitive war-room.

slides.title: Q3 beat plan, but growth is concentrated and SMB economics have broken
slides.speaker_notes: Frame the session: we beat plan but the composition of the beat changes the strategy. Two decisions are required today — the $2M reallocation and the $50K ARR floor. Set expectation that the war-room is the third action we'll discuss but it does not require board approval.

slides.title: Enterprise is carrying the company; SMB is destroying value at current CAC
body: Enterprise +34% YoY; SMB flat with CAC now 78% of first-year ACV
slides.speaker_notes: This is the deck's answer slide. State it cleanly and pause. The rest of the deck defends these two facts and motivates the three actions. Likely board pushback: 'Are we abandoning SMB?' — answer: no, we are restructuring it to be profitable.
slides.rationale: Single-insight emphasis at the top so the board has the punchline before the evidence.

slides.title: Revenue grew 12% to $48M, but 100% of growth came from enterprise
slides.strap: Enterprise added $5.1M YoY; SMB contributed zero net growth
body: Total revenue $48M, beating plan by 4% ($1.8M)
Enterprise revenue +34% YoY, now 77% of book
SMB revenue flat at $11M for third straight quarter
New-customer acquisition down 8% across both segments
slides.speaker_notes: Walk through the headline beat, then immediately decompose it. The point is that the consolidated number masks a binary outcome: one engine running hot, one engine stalled. Reference the CFO pack page 4 for the segment waterfall.

slides.title: Diagnosis: three pressures are reshaping the funnel
slides.speaker_notes: Transition. The three pressures are: (1) SMB unit economics, (2) enterprise health as the contrast case, (3) Beta competitive pressure at the top of funnel. Tell the board we will take each in turn before landing the response.

slides.title: SMB unit economics have inverted: CAC now exceeds first-year contract value
slides.strap: CAC up 19% to $14K against an $18K average ACV — and churn is concentrated here
body: SMB CAC rose 19% QoQ to $14K per new customer
Average first-year SMB contract is $18K — 78% consumed by CAC
Churn ticked to 4.2%, concentrated in sub-$50K ARR cohort
Payback period now exceeds contract length for ~40% of new SMB deals
slides.speaker_notes: This is the core justification for the $50K ARR floor. The math: at $14K CAC and 4.2% churn concentrated below $50K, we are acquiring customers we cannot retain long enough to recoup acquisition cost. Expected pushback: 'SMB is a feeder for enterprise expansion' — counter with the data that sub-$50K cohort almost never expands.

slides.title: Enterprise remains healthy — 124% NRR and 8-month payback
slides.strap: The segment we'd starve to fund SMB is the one with proven compounding economics
body: Net revenue retention 124% on accounts above $250K ARR
CAC steady at $42K with 8-month payback period
Enterprise revenue +34% YoY, now $37M annualized
Expansion within existing accounts contributed $4.1M of the $5.1M lift
slides.speaker_notes: Contrast slide. The point is to show that the marginal dollar in enterprise compounds — 124% NRR means each cohort grows itself. Reference the cohort waterfall in the appendix. This sets up the ROI comparison on slide 8.

slides.title: Beta is winning 59% of large deals and stretching our sales cycle by 16 days
slides.strap: Win rate on >$250K ARR deals fell from 58% to 41% in one quarter
body: Win rate vs Beta on >$250K deals dropped from 58% to 41%
Sales cycle lengthened from 47 to 63 days (+34%)
Pipeline conversion fell from 22% to 17% across all segments
Beta now appears in 71% of competitive enterprise evaluations
slides.speaker_notes: This is the motivation for the war-room. We are still growing enterprise 34%, but we are leaving deals on the table — every point of win rate recovered against Beta is roughly $1.2M in incremental ARR at current pipeline volume. Likely question: 'Is this a product gap or a sales gap?' — answer: per loss-review data, 60% sales execution, 40% product positioning.

slides.title: The response: reallocate, raise the floor, and counter Beta
slides.speaker_notes: Transition to the recommendations. Three actions, two require board approval today, one is operational. Frame as an integrated package — each action reinforces the others.

slides.title: Shifting $2M from SMB marketing to enterprise demand-gen lifts ROI roughly 3x
slides.strap: Marginal dollar comparison based on trailing four-quarter blended performance
body_left: $2M generates ~143 customers, ~60% retained past year one
slides.speaker_notes: This is the financial heart of the recommendation. The 3x figure is conservative — it does not assume any win-rate recovery from the war-room. If the board challenges the assumptions, walk them to appendix B which shows the sensitivity analysis. Note that we are not zeroing SMB marketing — the residual $1.4M continues to fund the resized, $50K-floor SMB motion.
slides.rationale: Comparison IS the point — SMB vs enterprise marginal ROI side-by-side is the cleanest way to justify the shift.

slides.title: A $50K ARR floor removes the cohort driving 4.2% churn and negative CAC payback
slides.strap: Effective Q4; existing customers grandfathered; channel partners notified November 1
body: Sub-$50K cohort drove 78% of Q3 churn events
Floor removes ~35% of new SMB deal volume but only ~12% of SMB revenue
Remaining SMB deals project to $32K average ACV, 2.3x current CAC
Frees ~6 AE-quarters of capacity to redeploy to mid-market
slides.speaker_notes: Justify the floor with the churn concentration data. Anticipate two objections: (1) 'We are walking away from a market' — response: we are walking away from unprofitable acquisition, not the segment. (2) 'What about strategic logos?' — response: floor includes a CRO-approved exception process, capped at 5 deals per quarter.

slides.title: Competitive war-room targets reclaiming 10+ points of win rate against Beta
slides.strap: Cross-functional standup; product, sales, and marketing; first readout in 60 days
body: Dedicated team: 2 product, 2 sales eng, 1 PMM, 1 RevOps
Battlecard refresh and loss-review program live by week 3
Three product gaps identified in loss reviews; fixes scoped for Q1
Each 1-point win-rate recovery worth ~$1.2M ARR at current pipeline
slides.speaker_notes: This action does not require board approval but the board should understand it as part of the integrated response. The 10-point target would restore us to 51% win rate — still below the 58% peak but enough to add ~$12M to FY pipeline yield. Funded from existing budget; no incremental ask.

slides.title: Combined actions protect FY plan and restore SMB to profitable growth by Q2
body: Integrated impact: +$6M enterprise ARR, SMB CAC payback under 12 months by Q2
slides.speaker_notes: Close the argument before the ask. The three actions are mutually reinforcing: reallocation funds the engine that's working, the floor stops the bleeding, and the war-room defends the lead. Land the FY protection point — this is what the board cares about most.
slides.rationale: Second key_takeaway lands the integrated outcome before the explicit ask — narrative inflection point.

slides.title: Decisions requested: approve $2M reallocation, $50K ARR floor, and war-room standup
body: Approve $2M reallocation from SMB marketing to enterprise demand-gen, effective Q4
Approve $50K ARR floor for new SMB deals, effective October 1
Endorse competitive war-room standup; first board readout in 60 days
CFO to recut FY forecast by November 15 reflecting approved changes
Return to board in Q1 with win-rate, churn, and ROI tracking against targets
slides.speaker_notes: Explicit asks. Pause after each for discussion. If the board defers the floor, recommend proceeding with the reallocation alone — but flag that the SMB churn drag will continue to mask the enterprise lift. Have the resolution language ready for the corporate secretary.
